A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAGE-3D research work. All main-text pages, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F were readable and comparable; the appendices are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original navigation evaluations, model training results, rendering/convergence measurements and sensitivity analyses in Tables 2–6 and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including SAGE-Bench evaluations and transfer experiments on VLN-CE R2R Val-Unseen.

M1.justification: Object-level semantic grounding, the 3DGS–mesh physics representation, instruction generation and A*-based trajectory generation remain unchanged. No algorithm, model component or training objective is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same InteriorGS/SAGE-Bench coverage, high- and low-level VLN instructions, No-goal Navigation and VLN-CE transfer evaluation. No datasets, task categories or evaluation scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2, 4 and 5 retain the same comparator sets. Graying selected baseline scores changes their interpretation and presentation, not which models were evaluated.

E3.justification: The test splits, 500k-pair training subset, model configurations, metrics and training settings remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendix A. The new caveat about low-success models does not revise the documented testing procedures or metric calculations.

E4.justification: The instruction-level comparisons, scene/sample-size study, evaluation-slice analyses, navigation cases and appendix visual comparisons are retained. The new failure-behavior explanation is not accompanied by an additional diagnostic experiment or case study.

E5.justification: Run/seed documentation and uncertainty presentation, including Figure 5's shaded bands, are unchanged. Table 2's new wording about comparative significance concerns metric interpretability, not a statistical significance test.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes NaVILA-base's CR from 1.66 to 3.53, reversing its ordering against NaVILA-SAGE's unchanged 2.67. Figure 2 changes its asset count from 544k to 554k. Section 4.2 also newly reports random or repeated-action behavior among weak baselines; other experimental scores are retained.

T1.justification: The augmented POMDP formulation, semantic-map construction and mathematical definitions of CSR, ICP and PS remain unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The SAGE-3D, InteriorGS and SAGE-Bench contributions and the claimed 31% relative transfer improvement are retained. Changing 'three key advantages' to 'two' corrects the count of the two advantages already listed rather than removing a substantive claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly attributes some low-success baselines' behavior to failed instruction/environment understanding and random or repeated actions. It consequently qualifies their CR, ICP and PS scores as non-comparable, adding a substantive limitation to the previously unqualified presentation.

D1.justification: The abstract newly supplies a project-page address for accessing data and code. Implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, sampling procedures and prompts in the appendices remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked resources.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list and substantive related-work positioning remain unchanged. The related-work text only flows differently across pages.

P1.justification: Localized edits add the abstract's access statement and the metric caveat, and correct 'three' advantages to 'two.' The section sequence, overall narrative and appendix prose are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 adds gray metric values and an explanatory caption; Tables 2, 4 and 6 adjust bold emphasis. Existing Table 3/Figure 4 move to page 8 and Table 6/Figure 5 to page 9. Figure 2's asset label is revised; no displays are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The access pointer and explicit warning about misleading collision/smoothness comparisons improve usability and interpretive transparency. Figure 2's asset-count revision also aligns that label with the existing main text. These are limited reporting improvements: the CR revision is unexplained, and the new failure diagnosis receives no additional supporting analysis.
